talking_points.headline: Anthropic scraps blanket Claude data retention for a customer-held-data model — the governance bar for every bank AI vendor just moved
talking_points.context_html: Anthropic's new Enterprise Frontier Safeguards keeps misuse-detection scanning but moves the underlying activity logs into the customer's own cloud rather than Anthropic's, directly answering the objection regulated firms have raised about GenAI vendor data retention. Kate Jensen, who leads Anthropic's Americas business, said the design lets enterprises get the safety benefits "without having to compromise on their own privacy posture." For Adam, this is a template competitors and vendors alike will now be measured against as HSBC evaluates which LLM providers meet regulated-industry data-control requirements for Wealth Intelligence and future agentic rollouts.

talking_points.headline: Standard Chartered becomes the first G-SIB to offer institutional crypto trading in the UAE, widening the digital-asset gap with HSBC's tokenisation-only approach
talking_points.context_html: Standard Chartered now lets institutional clients trade Bitcoin and Ether spot through its existing FX platforms in the DIFC, extending the UK launch it pioneered in 2025. Rola Abu Manneh, CEO for UAE, Middle East and Pakistan at Standard Chartered, called it "a significant step in broadening our regulated digital asset proposition." HSBC's digital-asset strategy remains anchored in tokenised deposits and its forthcoming PayMe stablecoin — a deliberately narrower bet than StanChart's move into direct crypto-asset trading, and a live test of which approach institutional and private banking clients actually want.
source_links: StanChart first G-SIB on UAE crypto trading

talking_points.headline: Deloitte data shows a trust gap that could stall RM-facing AI rollouts: clients use gen AI but don't believe what it tells them
talking_points.context_html: Only 46% of banking customers trust gen-AI-generated information versus 79% who trust a bank's own website, even as most already use the tools — and over 40% of financial professionals have now personally encountered deepfake-enabled fraud attempts. Val Srinivas of Deloitte's Center for Financial Services co-authored the research underpinning the finding. For Adam, this is a direct data point for the change-execution case on Wealth Intelligence and any RM-facing GenAI tool: adoption metrics alone won't prove value if clients quietly discount what the AI tells them, and the deepfake trendline raises the bar on RM identity-verification controls.
source_links: Survey: bank customers use gen AI but don't trust it
Deloitte: deepfake banking fraud risk rising

AI & Technology.title: Anthropic launches Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, ending blanket Claude data retention
AI & Technology.summary: Anthropic unveiled Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), replacing its 30-day default data-retention policy with a model where Claude activity logs are scanned for misuse but stored in the customer's own cloud infrastructure rather than Anthropic's. The offering rolls out in phases from this autumn and will not change model behaviour, pricing or rate limits.

AI & Technology.title: Deloitte: bank customers use gen AI tools but still don't trust them with sensitive information
AI & Technology.summary: A Deloitte Center for Financial Services survey of roughly 2,600 banking customers found 72% are wary of sharing financial details with gen AI tools and only 46% trust AI-generated banking information, versus 79% who trust a bank's own website. Separately, Deloitte's fraud research found over 40% of financial professionals have already encountered deepfakes used in fraud attempts.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Standard Chartered becomes first G-SIB to offer institutional Bitcoin and Ether spot trading in the UAE
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Standard Chartered's DIFC-regulated entity began offering institutional clients spot Bitcoin and Ether trading integrated into its existing FX platforms, with settlement through a custodian of the client's choice. It is the first Global Systemically Important Bank to offer the capability in the UAE, extending a service it first launched in the UK in 2025.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: WealthAi launches AI-native platform for independent wealth advisers
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: WealthAi expanded its wealth-management operating system with a version aimed at independent advisers and smaller firms, bundling AI meeting notetaking, CRM, document generation and compliance monitoring into one platform. Beta firms reported routine client-administration time falling 60% and the platform can be deployed within days without replacing existing practice-management systems.

HSBC News.title: HSBC Asset Management adds sterling-hedged share classes to its Sukuk UCITS ETF
HSBC News.summary: HSBC Asset Management introduced GBP FX-hedged share classes for its HSBC Global Funds ICAV – Global Sukuk UCITS ETF, which had previously offered only USD-based classes. The move is aimed at UK defined-contribution pension clients seeking Shariah-compliant fixed income exposure without unhedged currency risk.

Regulatory & Markets.title: New York Fed's Williams: bond-yield surge reflects AI investment boom, not inflation panic
Regulatory & Markets.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said the recent rise in Treasury yields reflects strong investment demand tied to AI and data-centre buildout rather than runaway inflation, and that he is taking a wait-and-see approach on a September rate move. He described inflation expectations as "well-anchored" despite tariff- and Iran-war-linked price pressure.

Operations & Change.title: Bank of America, Wells Fargo and BNY detail how AI is reshaping day-to-day operations
Operations & Change.summary: Major US banks disclosed the operational scale of their AI rollouts: Bank of America said over 200,000 staff now use AI tools generating 400,000+ prompts a day, Wells Fargo said nearly 9 in 10 staff use its AI Teammate copilot, and BNY's CEO pointed to AI-driven productivity as a core value driver. McKinsey estimates AI could cut banking industry costs by up to 20%.
